reference.title: AT+MHTTPDLFILE HTTP Download File
reference.shortdesc: This commands is used to download data into the file system without creating instances.

row.entry: Syntax
Response
Test command AT+MHTTPDLFILE=?
If succeed: OK If fail: +CME ERROR: <err>
Set command AT+MHTTPDLFILE=<url>,<local_path>[,<progind>[,<range>[,<eof>[,<ssl_id>]]]]
If succeed: OK If fail: +CME ERROR: <err>
URC
Command Description

This command is a single-step operation without creating instances first. It executes a GET request and uses the default header. Requested header will be reported via +MHTTPURC: "header" without being stored in the file. Download progress will be reported as the URC form. When the server delivers data in Content-Length mode with a value of 0, download progress notifications will not be reported.
Parameter Description

<url>The resource path shall include the URL components, such as host, port and path. For instance, "http://example.com/abc.txt" or "http://example.com:8080/abc.txt". ML307G: If the http or https is not explicitly specified in the URL, HTTPS will be used as the default protocol.

<local_path>Local file path with its length being file system dependent.
ML302S/ML307S/ML302A/ML305A/ML307A/ML307G/ML307R/ML307B/ML307C/MR380R/MR380M: If the first character of <local_path> is a forward slash ("/"), the downloaded file will be stored in the path specified by the user; otherwise, it will be stored in the /etc/http_file/ directory.
ML305U/ML305M/ML307X/ML307Y: If <local_path> contains only a forward slash ("/"), the downloaded file will be stored at the user-specified path; If only a backslash ("\") or no slashes at all, the file will be saved under /etc/http_file/.
ML307Y: Directories occupy storage space. It is recommended to use single-level directories whenever possible.
<progind>The module reports download progress via URC when the downloaded data reaches the specified length with default 0. It will only report final download result without the progress.

<range>Resource download range (the server support required) refers to RFC2616 for details on the Range field. The format is a string, e.g., "bytes=500-900", which indicates the transmission of bytes 500 to 900 of the file, totaling 401 bytes.

<eof>File write Mode, default value: 0. When the <range> is not configured and <eof> is configured to 1, the module will automatically enable breakpoint resume transfer, which means if the download process is abnormally interrupted, the module will continue downloading from the point after the last received data upon the next request for the same file. If the file has already been fully downloaded, do not initiate another download in this mode, as it may cause download errors. Instead, either delete the existing file or download in overwrite mode. Before using the breakpoint resume feature, ensure that the previously downloaded data starts from the first byte. When <eof> is configured to 0, the system clears the original file content immediately upon opening the file (even if the newly downloaded file is actually empty). If a subsequent write failure occurs during the download due to insufficient storage space or other reasons, the original file content cannot be restored.

plentry.pd: Overwrite mode (Clear all existing content before writing new data)
Append mode (Write new data contiguously after existing content)

row.entry: <ssl_id>SSL context index specifies the SSL context used by the current instance. Valid range refers to the document "SSL User Manual". When this parameter is not set, SSL is not enabled. When it is set, SSL is enabled. ML302A/ML305A/ML307A/ML307G/ML307S/ML305U/ML305M/ML307R/ML307B/ML307C/ML307X/ML307Y: <ssl_id> parameter range 0-5.
<downloaded>The downloaded length.
<content_length>Total download length. If the server response uses Chunked mode, intermediate progress reports will display 0.
<percent>Download progress percentage. If the request response is Chunked mode, intermediate progress reports will display 0. When transmission is completed, it will display 100.
<entity_length>Total length of the downloaded file. Valid when <range> is specified and the server responds with the Content-Range field.
Example

Download into the file. AT+MHTTPDLFILE="http://120.27.12.119:10080/get","/test.txt" OK +MHTTPURC: "header",0,200,225,HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx/1.18.0 Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2021 02:46:45 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 145 Connection: keep-alive Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true +MHTTPDLFILE: 145,145,100Download the file to the user-specified local path. AT+MHTTPDLFILE="http://120.27.12.119:10080/get","/test.txt" OK +MHTTPURC: "header",2,200,225,HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx/1.18.0 Date: Fri, 09 Sep 2022 09:39:04 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 189 Connection: keep-alive Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true +MHTTPDLFILE: 189,189,100 AT+MFLIST="/" +MFLIST: "/test.txt",189 OKDownload the file to the /etc/http_file/ path. AT+MHTTPDLFILE="http://120.27.12.119:10080/get","test.txt" OK +MHTTPURC: "header",2,200,225,HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx/1.18.0 Date: Fri, 09 Sep 2022 09:40:13 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 189 Connection: keep-alive Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true +MHTTPDLFILE: 189,189,100 AT+MFLIST="/etc/http_file/" +MFLIST: "/etc/http_file/test.txt",189 OK
